observation_summary: The complex tanh and tan functions return NaN instead of the expected asymptotic values when the input real or imaginary parts are large.
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because the mathematical implementation of the complex tanh and tan functions uses intermediate calculations (sinh/cosh) that overflow to infinity when the real or imaginary parts are large. This results in an 'infinity/infinity' operation, which produces NaN. The fix introduces threshold checks to return the expected asymptotic values (1.0 or -1.0 for tanh, and 0.0 +/- 1.0i for tan) when the input magnitude is large enough to cause overflow, thereby avoiding the unstable calculation.
